title: Arrive, a haircut, Asakusa at night
anchor: TORNADO in Omotesando from 17:30, then Senso-ji lit up after dark and dinner on Hoppy Street.
notes: Land 14:45. The Skyliner reaches Keisei-Ueno in about 41 minutes; the hotel is a 10-minute walk.

Hair at TORNADO in Omotesando, not booked yet: book today on Hot Pepper Beauty, or call 03-6804-2517 (English OK). Clara at 17:30 for the cut, colour and treatment (¥18,450, about 2.5 hours): the latest start that menu allows on a Friday, as the salon closes at 20:00. Brett at 18:30 for a cut (¥5,850, about an hour).

Clara goes straight from Keisei-Ueno: the Ginza line from Ueno (G16) to Omotesando (G02), no change, about 25 minutes, then 3 minutes from exit A2. Brett takes both bags to the hotel, then the Ginza line from Suehirocho (G14). If the flight is late, ring the salon: the coupons allow no same-day cancellation, and more than 10 minutes late can cancel the booking.

After the salon: the Ginza line from Omotesando (G02) straight to Asakusa (G19), about 30 minutes. Senso-ji's main hall and five-storey pagoda are lit from sunset until 23:00, without the daytime crowds.
Dinner on Hoppy Street (煮込み通り) by Senso-ji: beef-tendon and offal stews at outdoor tables, walk-in. Home: the Ginza line from Asakusa (G19) to Suehirocho (G14), no change.

Clara's Roppongi evening moves to Wednesday: the Mori Art Museum closes at 17:00 today (the museum's own site), and the salon takes the Louvre's slot. The Louvre show (not booked) drops; it runs until 13 Dec.
Or Roppongi tonight instead of Asakusa, as Clara first planned: the Hills Christmas Market is open until 21:00 and the Keyakizaka lights until 23:00.

title: Ginkgo, cats, Shimokita, Bazooka F
anchor: 神宮外苑いちょう並木 at 07:30, before the Saturday crush.
notes: 07:05 Ginza line from Suehirocho (G14) to Gaienmae (G03), no change, about 20 minutes.
The avenue was in full colour on 18 Nov, and the leaves start to fall around 2 Dec. This year the picture gallery at the end is under scaffolding, and there is no Christmas market at Gaien.
Ginkgo first, Gotokuji second: the avenue is shoulder to shoulder by 11:00, the cats will still be there at 09:30.
To Gotokuji: Ginza line to Shibuya, Den-en-toshi line to Sangenjaya, then the Setagaya tram to Miyanosaka. About 40 minutes.

After Gotokuji: the Setagaya tram from Miyanosaka to Shoin-jinja-mae, a few stops back toward Sangenjaya, for SOUEN at 11:00, Sakurai's casual tea bar (walk-in, closed Wednesdays). Then the tram to Sangenjaya and a 20-minute walk up Chazawa-dōri to Shimokitazawa.

Shimokitazawa from 12:30: a curry top-100 lunch (Kyu Yamu-tei Shimokita-so, KALPASI or PANNYA; expect a queue), then vintage, then MATCHA PASSPORT at 14:15. Most shops open around noon and many take cash only.

Sunset from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's free 45th-floor observatory: at about 15:30 take the Odakyu line from Shimokitazawa straight to Shinjuku (about 10 minutes), then walk about 10 minutes from the west exit, in time for the 16:30 sunset. Last entry 21:30. After dark the projection mapping plays on the building until about 21:30, free. Shibuya Sky instead only if a slot is left (not booked).

17:45 BEAMS JAPAN, five floors of made in Japan, open until 20:00 (moved here from Wednesday). If you got Shibuya Sky instead: Louis Vuitton Shibuya Men's holiday trains, Shibuya Loft or Chatei Hatō, then the JR Yamanote line to Shinjuku, about 7 minutes.
Dinner booked: Bazooka F, Nishi-Shinjuku 7-15-5, at 19:45. Charcoal yakiniku; the signature is the Bazooka harami. A 5–6 minute walk from Shinjuku's west exit.

Home: a nightcap at Omoide Yokochō by the west exit, or in Golden Gai's tiny bars across the station in Kabukicho, then the Oedo line from Shinjuku-nishiguchi straight to Ueno-okachimachi, near the hotel.

title: Todai ginkgo, the Japan Cup, Rikugien
anchor: The Japan Cup at 15:40, tickets won. Rikugien lit up after the races.
notes: Morning: Todai's ginkgo avenue to Yasuda Auditorium, quiet on a Sunday, then Nezu Shrine's tunnel of torii and Kayaba Coffee, each about 15 minutes' walk on.

Japan Cup tickets won: general admission, ¥1,000 each. The time on the ticket is the earliest you can go in (JRA staggers entry from 8:00 to 10:00); after it, come whenever you like. Show the QR ticket from the JRA booking site (from midnight; a screenshot works) at the main, west or east gate. Whoever won should send the second ticket on with チケット分配 before the day, as JRA asks.
Getting there: Shinjuku, then the Keio line to Fuchukeiba-seimonmae, about 35 minutes. Leave Kayaba by about 10:00. In by 13:00 to see the paddock; the race goes at 15:40.

Eat and drink at the infield gourmet festival. After the race: Ichiro's talk show, a special horse show, and a happy hour at the gourmet festival with ramen and beer half price. JRA expects the cash betting windows to jam in the afternoon, passages to be closed off when crowded, and phone signal to be patchy.
Rikugien: 18:00–20:30, last entry 19:30, ¥1,000 online or ¥1,200 cash. From the races: the Keio line back to Shinjuku, then the JR Yamanote line to Komagome. Then Tokiwa Shokudo, one stop away.
After Rikugien, instead of Tokiwa: Takokyu, a 14-seat oden counter in Yushima since 1904, open on Sundays. In winter arrive after 20:15; cash only; call 03-3831-5088 from 12:00 that day.
Clara's original afternoon (MOT, fukagawa-meshi, Mameya Kakeru, Kiyosumi Teien) gives way to the races.

title: teamLab, Daikanyama, Yokohama
anchor: teamLab at 11:00, the Dior Bamboo Pavilion after lunch, then Yokohama's Christmas market at dusk.
notes: A slow start after the races. 09:30 Hibiya line from Naka-Okachimachi straight to Kamiyacho, about 20 minutes; teamLab is two minutes from exit 5.
10:00, before teamLab: a tea tasting at SABOE in Azabudai Hills, or Kuro Mame in Toranomon, where the barista picks your coffee.
teamLab booked for 11:00. Allow 1.5–2.5 hours.
About 13:00 Hibiya line from Kamiyacho to Naka-Meguro, direct. Daikanyama is about 10 minutes' walk up; Onibus Coffee is a minute from the station.

Daikanyama: a late lunch at Have More Curry (curry top 100), then the Dior Bamboo Pavilion (daily 11:00–19:00, walk-in; Café Dior needs an online booking by 23:00 the day before, not booked), then designer resale at Hedy and Eva Fashion Art. Monday hours for Hedy and Eva aren't checked.
15:45 Toyoko line from Daikanyama straight through to Bashamichi, about 40 minutes, in time for the Air Cabin at about 16:30.
Monday is the market's calmest day, and the cable car catches sunset around 16:30.
Home: JR from Sakuragicho to Okachimachi or Akihabara, about 50 minutes.
Or dinner back near the hotel instead of Noge: Namaiki, a yakiniku top-100 two blocks away, open until 23:30.

title: Kamakura and Enoshima
anchor: Hasedera's maples and Enoshima on a weekday, then omakase at Ginza Ichibun at 18:00.
notes: 07:30 leave. JR to Tokyo, then the Yokosuka line to Kita-Kamakura, about an hour.
Kamakura's maples are among the last in Japan to turn, holding into early December.
Lunch: shirasu-don, whitebait on rice.
Enoden from Kamakura to Hase is five minutes; the Great Buddha is five minutes' walk from Hasedera.
Hasedera's night illumination, if it's announced, now clashes with the 18:00 dinner: keep the daytime order.
To dinner: Odakyu from Katase-Enoshima to Shinjuku, about 70 minutes, then the Marunouchi line to Ginza; or JR from Fujisawa to Tokyo. Leave Enoshima by about 16:15, before the sunset.

Dinner booked on Tabelog: Ginza Ichibun's omakase. Everyone starts together at 18:00, for about two hours; ¥28,600; no overly casual clothes. Afterwards walk 12 minutes to Ginza station, then the Ginza line from Ginza (G09) to Suehirocho (G14), no change.

title: Gyoen, Sakurai's tea, Mori at night
anchor: Shinjuku Gyoen in the morning, Sakurai's tea counter at 14:00, designer resale from Harajuku to Aoyama, then the Mori Art Museum and Roppongi's lights.
notes: Nezu Museum is closed between exhibitions from 24 Nov to 5 Dec, garden included. This day replaces it.
09:00 Marunouchi line from Awajicho straight to Shinjuku-gyoemmae. ¥500.

About 11:00 the Fukutoshin line from Shinjuku-sanchome to Meiji-jingumae, two stops. Lunch at Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera by Omotesando, about ¥300 a plate, then Vintage Qoo before 14:00 to beat the crowd, and Kindal.
14:00 Sakurai's eight-seat tea counter, booked: a tea course served like an omakase, in Minami-Aoyama.
After Sakurai: RAGTAG on Cat Street, BEAMS and United Arrows in Jingumae 3-chome, then AURALEE's Aoyama store (12:00–20:00), and back down Omotesando under Fendi's 900,000 LEDs.

Evening, moved from Friday: the Mori Art Museum's Mariko Mori retrospective, open until 22:00 tonight (last entry 21:30), timed tickets online. The Ginza line from Omotesando to Aoyama-itchome, then the Oedo line to Roppongi. Then the Roppongi Hills Christmas Market (until 21:00) and the Keyakizaka lights (until 23:00).
Dinner at the market: glühwein, sausages and stollen. The old evening plans stay below as ideas: Ōi night racing, and the Nakameguro sushi counters and Bar Benfiddich, which need booking.

More evenings: Kinju, a yakiniku top-100 in Nakameguro open until 03:30; Nishio-san's Shizuoka oden in Shinjuku-sanchome before Benfiddich (same-day phone booking, cash). For a quiet night, Ishibashi's sukiyaki is a minute from Suehirocho (last order 20:00, cash only).

title: Tsukiji, the museum, Ginza, fly
anchor: Tsukiji's breakfast and market, the Daitoku-ji show, Ginza's brand spaces and Marunouchi's lights, then Narita for the 22:00 flight.
notes: 07:30 check out and leave the bags at the front desk; collect them at 17:30.

Tsukiji is open today (it shuts on 29 Nov and 2 Dec). Hibiya line from Naka-Okachimachi to Tsukiji, direct. Breakfast at Tsumugi in Tsukiji Hongwanji at 08:00: 16 small plates, rice porridge and miso, ¥2,200 with tea. Not booked: half of its 110 places a day are bookable online, the other half are walk-in.
09:00 the outer market and Tsukiji Uogashi: tamagoyaki at Yamachō, a matcha whisk at Yamanoi Shōten. Eating while walking is banned: eat at the stall. Most shops close around 14:00.

The Daitoku-ji show is in its last week: Muqi's Dragon and Tiger and a National Treasure Ido tea bowl. Hibiya line from Tsukiji to Ueno, direct, for 10:15. Swap: Hamarikyu's teahouse instead, 10 minutes' walk from Tsukiji.
Sushi lunch in Ginza at 12:00, walk-in: Nemuro Hanamaru (Tokyu Plaza Ginza 10F; put your name down and wander) or Kaiten Toyama. Hibiya line from Ueno to Ginza, direct.

Afternoon in Ginza: Hermès Le Forum (Ann Veronica Janssens, free), Dover Street Market, Louis Vuitton's Le Café V, then tea and wagashi at HIGASHIYA GINZA at 15:00 and G.Itoya on the way to Marunouchi.

Naka-dōri's 1.2 km of lit trees come on at 16:00. On Gyoko-dōri, between Tokyo station and the palace, a Christmas market with Harry Potter decorations and, from 27 Nov, 15 Christmas huts; the Hogwarts Snow Tree is in Marucube, Marunouchi Building 1F. Tokyo to Akihabara is four minutes.
Leave the hotel by 18:15 for Narita, 30 minutes earlier than before, for the tax-refund kiosk: Skyliner from Keisei-Ueno, about 41 minutes.
With the Japan Cup on Sunday, Kuramae and 2k540 can go to Clara's morning on Fri 4 Dec.
